screening_decisions.reason: This is a review article discussing drug interactions in epilepsy therapy, not a controlled clinical trial. No randomization or control groups mentioned.
This appears to be a case report describing a single patient's experience with dexamethasone-phenytoin interaction. Not a controlled clinical trial with randomization.
This is a randomized controlled trial with 200 patients randomly allocated to two groups (PHT vs no PHT/placebo). Open-label design with control group. Meets all selection criteria.
This is a prospective observational study evaluating risk of postoperative seizures and EEG findings. No randomization or control groups mentioned.
This is a practice parameter/guideline document from the American Academy of Neurology, not a controlled clinical trial.

This describes 100 patients in a therapy protocol comparing those who received prophylactic anticonvulsants vs not, but does not explicitly state randomization. Appears to be observational within a protocol.
Explicitly stated as a retrospective study. Does not meet the criterion of being a controlled clinical trial with random allocation.
Double-blind randomized trial of phenytoin for postoperative epilepsy prevention. Includes patients with meningioma and metastasis (brain tumors) among other conditions. Has placebo control group.
Randomized controlled trial with 284 patients with brain metastases. Diazepam vs no diazepam for contrast-associated seizure prevention. Meets selection criteria.
Single-arm study analyzing 150 patients receiving oxcarbazepine. No control group or randomization mentioned. Observational design.
This is a letter to the editor/commentary discussing drug interactions, not a controlled clinical trial.
Double-blind randomized trial with placebo control (101 phenytoin vs 102 placebo). Tests phenytoin for postoperative epilepsy prevention in craniotomy patients including those with brain tumors.
Review article discussing mechanisms and management of seizures in brain tumor patients. Not a controlled clinical trial.
Prospective randomized series of glioma patients receiving diazepam vs no diazepam for contrast-associated seizure prevention. Meets selection criteria.
Randomized controlled trial with 189 patients receiving phenytoin vs 185 placebo controls. Tests prophylactic anticonvulsants for postcraniotomy seizure prevention.
This trial compares radiation therapy vs no radiation therapy, not antiepileptic drugs. Wrong intervention for this review.
Survey study of practitioner practices and opinions. Not a controlled clinical trial.
Survey study of neurosurgeons' practice patterns. Not a controlled clinical trial.
Prospective randomized unblinded trial with 100 brain tumor patients randomized to anticonvulsants vs no anticonvulsants. Meets selection criteria.
Meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials, not a primary clinical trial itself. Secondary research synthesis.
This is a review article providing guidelines for family physicians, not a controlled clinical trial. It uses illustrative clinical cases and literature review, not randomized allocation.

While this study has random allocation (20 patients randomized to 10mg/kg vs 15mg/kg phenytoin), it does NOT have a placebo or observation control group. Both groups received active phenytoin treatment at different dosages. The selection criteria require placebo or observation in control groups.
This is a meta-analysis reviewing 30 publications and pooling results from six controlled studies. It is not itself a primary controlled clinical trial with random allocation.

This is an observational study of 234 consecutive patients attending an outpatient clinic. There is no random allocation or control group. Patients were simply examined and their seizure patterns documented.

This is explicitly described as a 'retrospective analysis' of 195 patients. There is no random allocation; patients either received prophylactic anticonvulsants or did not based on clinical decisions, not random assignment.

This study describes 128 patients where 41 were given AEDs and 22 were not treated among those without preoperative seizures. There is no mention of random allocation; this appears to be an observational comparison of treated vs untreated patients.
This is a review article examining existing data on four topics related to anticonvulsant prophylaxis. It is not a controlled clinical trial with random allocation.
This is an observational series describing 23 of 538 patients who had seizures after craniotomy. There is no random allocation or control group; it is a descriptive case series.
This is explicitly described as a 'retrospective review of charts' of 65 consecutive patients. There is no random allocation or control group.

This is a prospective, stratified, randomized, double-blind trial comparing phenytoin vs sodium valproate. While it meets the randomization and blinding criteria, BOTH groups received active anticonvulsant treatment. There is NO placebo or observation control group, which is required by the selection criteria.

This is an observational study of 81 patients with brain metastasis from melanoma. Patients were grouped by treatment approach (RT alone, RT+surgery), but there is no random allocation. The comparison of prophylactic vs non-prophylactic anticonvulsants is observational.

This is a randomized controlled trial where 276 patients were randomized to carbamazepine, phenytoin, OR NO TREATMENT. The 'no treatment' arm serves as an observation control group, meeting the selection criteria requirement for 'placebo or observation in the control groups'. This study directly addresses seizure prophylaxis in patients undergoing craniotomy.

This is explicitly described as a 'randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study' comparing divalproex sodium vs placebo in patients with newly diagnosed brain tumors who had not previously had seizures. This perfectly meets all selection criteria: random allocation, blinding, AND placebo control group.
